newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power coops see need to band amid competition.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power coops see need to band amid competition.

text.p: U.S. electric cooperatives are feeling a growing need to join together in the face of deregulation and increasing competition in the power industry.
"It came about because of competitiveness of the business. It allows us to work together to save money," Richard Byrne, president of the Buckeye Power Inc co-operative told Reuters.
The Columbus, Ohio based cooperative is a member of Alliance for Cooperative Energy Services (ACES) whose formation was announced on Thursday.

The group of nine generation and transmission cooperatives provide wholesale electric power to distribution cooperatives serving nearly nine million customers in ten states including Florida, Georgia, Alabama, Kentucky, North Carolina, Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan and New Jersey.

ACES hopes to achieve a level of efficiency and an economy of scale to compete with the biggest investor-owned utilities, which are also merging with each another, said Bryne, who is also president of ACES.

An ACES member with surplus capacity to produce power could transmit extra power to other alliance participants, which in turn could eliminate the need to build new generating capacity, according to Bryne.
ACES aims to achieve eventual savings of 10-20 percent for customers, he said.
The group also will develop coordinated marketing efforts, Bryne said.
"We're going to try to buy as one...We can collectively work as a marketer ourselves," he said.
In 1995, ACES' nine cooperatives had combined revenues of $3.5 billion on electricity sales of 75 billion kilowatt hours (KWh).

In contrast, Buckeye's Columbus neighbor, American Electric Power Co, which is considered the second biggest U.S. electricity provider among utilities, collected operating revenues of $5.67 billion on sales of 120.7 billion KWh in 1995.
Byrnes said ACES plans to bring other cooperatives with generation and transmission assets into the organization.
He noted the alliance would not prohibit members from working in other joint ventures, adding ACES cooperatives in the northern U.S. have been seeking to partner with investor-owned utilities.
